newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Philippines Yankee up next.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Philippines Yankee up next.

text.p: The long-awaited Yankee bond for the central bank of the Philippines is expected to launch when U.S. markets open today, bankers said on Tuesday.
Bankers said the bond is expected to be launched on Tuesday in New York and priced on Wednesday.

Central bank governor Gabriel Singson confirmed earlier today that Salomon Brothers had been chosen to lead manage the bond issue. In April, the central bank decided to postpone its Yankee bond just hours before its launch, citing poor market conditions.

Like the postponed issue, the new bond will be launched in two tranches. Syndicate managers in Asia said that price talk for the 30-year bond is 185 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries, while the 100-year bond is expected to price at 197.5 basis points over the benchmark.
Price talk on the previous 30-year issue was 212 to 225 basis points over Treasuries at the time the bond was postponed, reflecting a poor market for emerging market credits.
The Philippines foreign currency bond issues are rated Ba1 by Moody's Investors Service and BB-plus by Standard and Poor's Corp, below investment grade.
Central bank governor Gabriel Singson said Salomon had beaten four other banks bidding for the mandate.

The central bank had invited all six banks involved in the original deal - Salomon Brothers, Citibank NA, Morgan Stanley, Merrill Lynch, JP Morgan and ING Barings -- to rebid, but Singson did not say which bank had dropped out.
Singson declined to divulge details of the bond, but called the pricing "a very good spread for us."
Bankers said that at 185 basis points, the new issue would be tightly priced. They said the Philippines oustanding bond due in 2016 was trading around 180-185 basis points over the benchmark.
"It's an aggressive deal," said one syndicate manager.
Another banker called that spread "pricey."
"If we were in a bull market, they could price the deal on top of the secondaries, but we're not so the deal may not have enough juice," he said.
Syndicate managers said they did not expect the new bond to act as a new benchmark, with many predicting that the spread would widen after launch.

Bankers said they expected the 30-year tranche to be US$400 million in size and the century tranche to be US$100 million in size. Last week, Singson said the bond would be less than US$750 million in size, he said.
Salomon Brothers was not immediately available for comment.
A number of Asian issuers are pondering Yankee bonds.
From South Korea, Shinhan Bank and Pusan Bank are eyeing the U.S. market, as is Pohang Iron and Steel (POSCO).
There is talk South Korea's City of Taegu is considering a Yankee.
Bankers said Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand, which recently pulled a floating rate note issue, is pondering a Yankee or samurai issue.
In new issues, AAA-rated BNG of the Netherlands launched a US$1 billion Euro-Asian bond. The five-year issue will be priced to yield 12 basis points over Treasuries.

ABN AMRO, Goldman Sachs and Nomura International were the lead managers. Bankers in Hong Kong said the bond likely attracted interest from regional central banks and some institutional investors, mostly in Japan.
In other news, Thailand's state-run property support agency Property Loan Management Organisation (PLMO) said it will seek government permission to raise funds in foreign markets.
